_doc: OPS-GIT-IDENTITY-CANONICALIZE-W1 — allowlist for scripts/check-author-identity.sh. Every exemption row carries its OWN reason; a reason living only in a comment or in prose gets 'fixed' by a future wave enforcing the contract. Missing, empty or unparseable ⇒ AUTHOR_IDENTITY_VERDICT=INDETERMINATE, exit 3 — never a pass. WE author this file, so empty is a defect in our config, not a fact about the world.
_semantics: ALLOWLIST, not deny-list: an email absent from `allowed` FAILS. `denied` exists so the guard NAMES a known-bad address in its output instead of merely failing to match it — the diagnostic difference between 'not allowed' and 'this is the Gmail we retired on 2026-08-09'.
_scope: core.hooksPath is set --local in crypto-quant-signal-mcp, so this pre-commit block governs that repo and its linked worktrees ONLY. CI identities (ci@algovault.com, github-actions@github.com) and host identities (funnel-snapshot@algovault.com, algovault@hetzner.local, editorial@algovault.com) author commits on machines where this hook is not installed, and are deliberately NOT allowlisted here: allowlisting an identity this guard can never legitimately see would weaken it for zero benefit. If one ever appears locally, that is a real finding.

promotion.reason: REPORT-first because a guard that blocks on day one wedges the fleet, and a guard permanently stuck in REPORT is decoration. 7 days rather than the usual 14+ because remediation here is INSTANT AND GLOBAL — CH2 fixed inheritance in one file and CH3 deleted 11 local overrides in one pass — unlike gate-staleness, whose per-worktree healing depends on each checkout rebasing and measurably did not converge over 24h.
promotion.criterion: BOTH conditions, never collapsed into one: max_violations must be 0 across the observation window AND today must be >= not_before. A numeric bar alone can be met on day one by a machine nobody committed from; a date bar alone promotes a guard that is still firing. Every run appends its verdict to $GIT_COMMON_DIR/algovault-author-identity.log so the promotion decision is MEASURED from that log, not asserted.
promotion._measure_from_reason: OPS-AUTHOR-IDENTITY-PROMOTE-W1 measured the ledger and found 4 FAIL + 3 INDETERMINATE rows, ALL bearing one timestamp (2026-08-09T10:55:51Z) and one repo root (the worktree that BUILT this guard). They are the previous wave's AC4.2/4.3/4.4 evidence — the acceptance tests that PROVED the guard can fail, run against the real common-dir before the throwaway-repo rule existed. Proving a guard can fail necessarily writes FAIL rows, so THE INSTRUMENT CONTAINS ITS OWN CALIBRATION. `max_violations: 0` measured over the whole ledger therefore conflates CALIBRATION with OPERATION — it measures the wrong population, and because those rows never age out the criterion as written could NEVER be satisfied, in perpetuity. Same defect class as V1's AC11. measure_from cuts the calibration rows out of the population; it does not erase them, and the ledger is never touched. Explicitly REJECTED alternative: raising max_violations to 4. That bakes the calibration count into the threshold, so 4 REAL violations would also pass — a window SEPARATES the two populations, a raised bar MERGES them.
promotion._min_rows_in_window_reason: A window with no sample floor is a free pass: set measure_from to yesterday and the criterion is trivially satisfiable by an empty window — the vacuity hole in the shape of a date. Fewer than min_rows_in_window rows after the cut is INDETERMINATE, never READY: too few observations is 'we have not looked', which is not 'we looked and it was clean'. 30 matches the house convention (report_class_promotion.runs_required, mode2_promotion.runs_required) and 65 rows were available at flip time, so it was satisfiable on the day it shipped rather than aspirational.
promotion._shape_note: This block deliberately does NOT match the {runs_required, escalate_after} shape that scripts/lib/promotion-bound.mjs asserts on freshness_promotion, report_class_promotion and mode2_promotion. Two criterion shapes exist in this repo and the divergence is INTENTIONAL: {runs_required, escalate_after} measures RUNS against an ESCALATION DATE; {max_violations, not_before, measure_from, min_rows_in_window} measures VIOLATIONS against a START BOUND. Do not 'unify' them — assertPromotionBound would throw on this block, and the unification would be the same mistake as collapsing claudemd-claim-config's two criteria with two owners into one.
promotion._reader: scripts/check-author-identity.sh --measure-promotion. measure_from and min_rows_in_window are NOT decorative: that flag reads them, counts in-window FAIL rows and prints PROMOTION_MEASURE_VERDICT=READY|BLOCKED|INDETERMINATE (exit 0/1/3). Dead config is config with no reader, and this repo's law says every field has >=1 live consumer. NOTE: this block has NO JavaScript consumer, so assertInstrumentIndependence is NOT called on it by any gate — its enforcement is tests/unit/promotion-independence.test.ts, which discovers it by scanning ops/*.json and runs on the existing pre-push vitest gate. That is deliberate and is why this wave needed no hook change.

instrument.population: Verdict rows appended to $GIT_COMMON_DIR/algovault-author-identity.log, one per pre-commit invocation of this gate.
instrument.written_by: scripts/check-author-identity.sh — the subject of this very criterion.
instrument.rederive: Bucket `git log --all --format='%H%x09%ae%x09%ct'` by AUTHOR email against allowed[] and out_of_scope_identities[], comparing INTEGER EPOCH SECONDS against measure_from — never an ISO string, because %cI carries each commit's own UTC offset and a lexicographic compare silently mis-buckets every non-UTC commit. The ledger is a CACHE of that answer, not the answer: commits are written by git, a deliberate run of this gate creates none, and the same verdict is therefore recomputable over any window at any time without reading the ledger at all. Measured at OPS-PROMOTION-INSTRUMENT-INDEPENDENCE-W1 Plan Mode, this re-derivation returned READY over the identical window in which the ledger returned BLOCKED — the difference being exactly the one manually-written FAIL row that HALTed OPS-AUTHOR-IDENTITY-PROMOTE-W1.
instrument.reason: B rather than C because the re-derivation above is real, stated and executable TODAY — it was run before this grade was assigned, not asserted alongside it. B rather than A only until CH2 of this wave lands: the ledger is still what --measure-promotion reads, so the primary population is still one this gate writes. CH2 re-points the flag at git history, at which point this block becomes grade A and `rederive` is REMOVED rather than left behind. Without the rederive field this block would be grade C — the ledger would be the sole record, and a deliberate run with GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=test@test.local can MANUFACTURE a violation that never occurred in operation, which is precisely what happened on 2026-08-16T04:42:06Z.
